title: Look Up with a Default
hints: A dictionary subscript can take a `default:` value for missing keys.
Put the five known codes in a dictionary, then map each code to its phrase or to the fallback text.
jsBridge: JS: `table[code] ?? \`Unknown (${code})\``. Swift's `??` is the same operator, but the left side must be an optional. Dictionary lookup returns `String?`, so the types line up perfectly.

compass.q: JS `??` and Swift `??` look identical. What happens in Swift if the left side isn't optional?
`dict[k] ?? fallback` vs `dict[k, default: fallback]`: when does each make sense, reading vs mutating?
The right side of `??` is an `@autoclosure`. When is it evaluated? Does an expensive fallback run when the key exists?
Mapping error codes to user-facing messages: should the table live in code, a `Localizable.xcstrings` catalog, or the server?
